title: Subnet mesh Terraform builder: VPC subnets, egress, endpoints, routing, and safe upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Produce a reusable Terraform module (module/subnet-mesh) that provisions a VPC subnet mesh designed for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support: AZ-aware subnet groups, configurable NAT or IGW egress per-subnet, interface and gateway VPC endpoints, route tables per-subnet-role, explicit route propagation toggles, and a pluggable health-checking hook set for automatic remediation and upgrade validation. The module should be opinionated enough to prevent insecure defaults but flexible for enterprise customers (tagging, CIDR scoping, endpoint policies). It must include upgrade hooks and a fallback plan so stateful upgrades (provider or resource schema changes) can be rolled back without data loss or requiring manual intervention in most common cases.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module available under modules/subnet-mesh with README and examples
Module supports two egress patterns: centralized NAT gw per-AZ and per-subnet IGW fallback
Automatic creation of VPC endpoints for S3, STS, ECR (configurable list)
Route table strategy: role-based route tables (control-plane, workload, infra) and a default mesh route policy
Health-check hooks emit metrics to our metrics pipeline and create alerts if route/endpoint anomalies detected
Canary upgrade flow: customers can opt into a canary plan that exercises new resource versions on a subset of subnets before full rollout
Backward-compatible variable schema with migration docs and at-most-once destructive operations
Unit and integration tests pass in our CI (plan/apply/destroy in ephemeral account)
technical_notes: Variables: cidr_block, az_map (map of AZ->subnet CIDR suffix), subnet_roles (list), egress_mode (nat_per_az | igw_by_role), endpoints (list)
Outputs: subnet_ids_by_role (map), route_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids, health_check_endpoint

Implementation: use aws_vpc, aws_subnet (count for AZs), aws_route_table_association, aws_internet_gateway, aws_nat_gateway, aws_vpc_endpoint (interface/gateway). Keep resource names deterministic to ease state moves.
State pinning: recommend separate state per-environment and a state migration helper script that renames resources when changing topology to avoid recreate where possible

Upgrade hooks: use a module-level null_resource with triggers invoking a Lambda/remote-exec to run post-change validations (route probe, DNS resolution, endpoint connectivity). These hooks must be opt-in via enable_upgrade_hooks variable.

Health checks: lightweight synthetic probes run from a control-plane subnet that validate egress paths, endpoint reachability, and correct route table associations. Failures emit a tag on the subnet and a Prometheus metric.
Testing harness: terratest or kitchen-terraform based tests that assert reachability and correct resources for both egress modes. Include a local smoke test script for solutions engineers.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy module to canary account with enable_upgrade_hooks=true and monitor for 48 hours
Phase 2: if canary OK, run non-destructive migration in staging with state snapshot and drift detection
Phase 3: gradual rollout to customer environments with communication doc and rollback commands
Failure rollback: provide documented terraform state move commands + helper script to rebind previously created resources to the prior module version
Post-upgrade: run health-check suite and mark upgrade as complete in a release note entry
test_plan: CI: terraform init/validate/plan and terratest suite on PR
Integration job: ephemeral sandbox account apply -> run probe scripts -> destroy (nightly)
Canary runbook: checklist for on-call and SEs with monitoring playbook and rollback commands
Chaos tests: simulate NAT gw failover and ensure route table healing triggers health-check remediation

risks: State drift during topology changes may cause resource replacement if not handled via migration helpers
Large accounts with existing networking might have overlapping route table naming and require manual state operations
Upgrade hooks executing remote checks require IAM permission scope that must be restricted to avoid privilege escalation
